interpretation: A universal identity-storage hypothesis was refuted.
In the v28 microbiome, removing fungal taxon labels did not reduce null-calibrated history retention; rank-abundance shape retained essentially all of the labeled-composition signal.
In the v30 grassland, removing functional-group labels removed about three quarters of the labeled-composition retained-history excess.
Assembly history can therefore be encoded through different present-state channels across systems: abundance architecture in one system and identity-to-rank assignment in another.
Shannon entropy retained significant history in both systems, confirming that identity-free abundance structure can itself carry historical information.
claim_boundary: Do not claim a universal identity-storage law.
Do not claim identity is irrelevant in the microbiome; v31 only shows that identity labels were unnecessary for retaining the tested history signal.
Do not claim grassland history is purely identity-based; rank abundance and Shannon entropy still retained nonzero history.
Do not present v31 as first discovery of functional convergence or compositional contingency.
